title: On Ultra $k$-Secure Sets in Graphs
summary: In a graph $G=(V,E)$, let $S$ be a non empty subset of $V$. For any $x\in S$, the vertex $x$ and its neighbors inside $S$ are defenders of $x$, whereas those lying outside $S$ are attackers on $x$. An attack on $S$ is an $|S|$-tuple of pairwise disjoint sets of attackers on vertices of $S$, whereas a defense is that of defenders. An attack on $S$ is defendable if $S$ has a defense, which provides at least as many defenders as attackers for each of its vertices. The set $S$ is a secure set if every attack on $S$ is defendable.
